subject: Geography
central_question: How do running water, groundwater, glaciers, waves, and wind produce distinctive erosional and depositional landforms and transform landscapes through time?
in_scope_units: Meaning, history, and evolution of landforms and landscapes.
Running-water erosion and deposition across youthful, mature, and gentler river courses.
River valleys, potholes, plunge pools, terraces, meanders, floodplains, levees, point bars, deltas, and alluvial fans.
Groundwater solution in limestone and karst landforms including sinkholes, uvalas, caves, stalactites, and stalagmites.
Glacial erosion and deposition including cirques, horns, arêtes, valleys, moraines, eskers, outwash plains, and drumlins.
Wave action and erosional and depositional forms of high rocky and low sedimentary coasts.
Wind and combined desert processes forming pediments, pediplains, playas, deflation hollows, dunes, and related forms.
banned_topics: Soil-profile horizons and Indian soil classification

known_pitfalls.claim: A meander is itself a separate landform.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter describes a meander as a channel pattern produced by lateral erosion and deposition.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every limestone depression is formed by mechanical erosion.
known_pitfalls.correction: Solution by groundwater is the dominant process in karst terrain.

known_pitfalls.claim: All glacial deposits are sorted like river alluvium.
known_pitfalls.correction: Glacial till is generally unsorted, while glacio-fluvial deposits may be sorted by meltwater.

known_pitfalls.claim: Wind alone creates every desert landform.
known_pitfalls.correction: Running water and sheet flooding also participate in desert landscape evolution.

known_pitfalls.claim: Coastal erosion and deposition are independent of sediment supply.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter stresses the coastal sediment budget and the balance among waves, currents, and supplied material.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Exercise 1(i): identify the stage dominated by vertical down-cutting.
NCERT Exercise 2(i): interpret incised meanders and alluvial meanders.
NCERT Exercise 2(ii): explain the evolution of valley sinks or uvalas.
NCERT Exercise 2(iv): locate and name linear glacial depositional forms.
NCERT Exercise 3(i): assess running water as a dominant geomorphic agent.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with EXERCISES 1(i–v), 2(i–v), 3(i–iii), followed by Project Work on local landforms, materials, and processes.
